2607.11327.title: PRISM Edit: One Vector for All Temporal Answers
2607.11327.paper_summary: Model editing keeps large language models (LLMs) up to date without retraining, but temporal facts expose a limitation of the prevailing locate-and-edit paradigm: an update is not always a replacement. When a fact changes, the new answer should become current while the old answer may remain correct in historical time contexts. Building on this insight, we use causal tracing to show that LLMs already support this distinction via a two-stage internal computation: early MLP layers retrieve a time-agnostic subject representation, and later layers modulate it with temporal context to yield the time-correct answer. Motivated by this finding, we introduce PRISM Edit, which optimizes a single polysemous representation across temporal contexts and leverages the model's inherent modulation pathway to route it to temporally correct predictions, without any architectural modification. We evaluate on TimeConflict, a new temporal editing benchmark we introduce, and on temporally augmented CounterFact. PRISM Edit improves over the best baseline by +23.3 Temporal Consistency (TC) and +33.7 Current Relative-time Score (CRS) on average while being more than 2x faster. Code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/AnonymousStudy972/PRISM-Edit.
2607.11327.paper_summary_zh: 模型編輯使大型語言模型（LLMs）在不重新訓練的情況下保持最新，但時間事實揭示了現行定位與編輯範式的局限性：更新並不總是替代。當事實發生變化時，新答案應該成為當前的，而舊答案在歷史時間背景下仍然可能是正確的。基於這一見解，我們使用因果追踪來展示LLMs已經通過兩階段的內部計算支持這一區別：早期的MLP層檢索一個與時間無關的主題表示，而後續層則用時間上下文對其進行調整，以產生時間正確的答案。受到這一發現的啟發，我們引入了PRISM Edit，它在時間上下文中優化單一的多義表示，並利用模型固有的調整通道將其引導至時間正確的預測，而無需任何架構修改。我們在TimeConflict上進行評估，這是一個我們引入的新時間編輯基準，以及在時間增強的CounterFact上。PRISM Edit在平均上比最佳基線提高了+23.3的時間一致性（TC）和+33.7的當前相對時間分數（CRS），同時速度超過2倍。代碼和數據可在https://github.com/AnonymousStudy972/PRISM-Edit公開獲得。
